title: Chain Rule: Tangent to a Composition
caption_md: The curve shows the composition $f(x) = (x^2+1)^3$. The dashed tangent line at $x=1$ has slope $6x(x^2+1)^2$ evaluated there, giving $6 \cdot 1 \cdot (1+1)^2 = 24$. Notice that if you forgot the inner derivative $g'(x)=2x$, you would get slope $3(x^2+1)^2 = 12$ — exactly half the correct value. The dotted curve shows the "outer-only" mistake $3(x^2+1)^2$ so you can see the wrong slope visually. The chain rule's extra factor of $g'(x)$ is what makes the tangent line match the actual curve.
